newsitem.title: USA: Powerful U.S. Air Force rocket blasts off.
newsitem.headline: Powerful U.S. Air Force rocket blasts off.

text.p: A powerful new U.S. Air Force Titan 4B rocket, developed at a cost of $1 billion, roared into space on Sunday, making its maiden flight.

The giant 20-storey rocket climbed skyward on a brilliant pillar of light from Cape Canaveral Air Station at 3:20 p.m. EST (2020 GMT). Nestled in its bulbous nose cone was a $200 million missile warning satellite.
"We have ignition and liftoff of the Titan 4B," said an Air Force launch commentator.

The new rocket is the result of a 9-year, $1 billion upgrade for the Titan 4, the workhorse of the U.S. military space program. It will primarily be used to launch spy satellites, but will also be employed by NASA in October to launch it's nuclear-powered Cassini probe to Saturn.

Improved and enlarged twin solid rocket motors, constructed from light-weight composite materials, have increased the rocket's cargo capacity by 25 percent. In its most powerful configuration the rocket can loft 48,000 lbs (21,770 kgs) into low earth orbit.
Aviation Week & Space Technology magazine described the rocket's maiden flight as "one of the most important Air Force space missions ever conducted."

Nine minutes after blastoff the missile warning satellite separated from the Titan. A two-stage rocket was to fire later to place the satellite into a stationary orbit 22,300 miles (35,900 kms) above the equator.
Similar satellites were used in the Gulf War to detect Iraqi Scud missile launches. It's sensitive instruments are capable of detecting the exhaust heat of a jet aircraft on afterburner.
